graders.name: check-declares-expected
graders.criteria: Pass if the final message reports a behavior check, run or proposed, that names what it exercised (the approval stop after triage) and states the expected or observed result, such as the agent stopping before any fix. A one-line summary suffices. Fail if it names no behavior check or only a consistency read of the text.

graders.name: gate
graders.criteria: Judge the edited `review-panel/SKILL.md`. After triage, the agent running the skill presents the findings, with their dispositions and proposed fixes, and stops; it applies only fixes the user has reviewed and approved. A fix outside what the user approved, such as one for a new finding from verification, needs fresh approval; an approved batch may include verifying and correcting those same fixes. Escalations still wait for the user's decision.

graders.name: keeps-rest
graders.criteria: Judge the edited `review-panel/SKILL.md`. Everything not about when fixes are applied keeps its meaning: scope resolution and its defaults, the brief, the roster, rivals and twin, the presets, the rules for voices and effort, merging, triage through `review-triage` inline, verification as a closed check with the two-pass cap, and the report contents.

graders.name: loads-evaluating-instructions
graders.description: Process check: The agent read `references/evaluating-instructions.md` of the skill, as the References table requires here.

graders.name: no-history
graders.criteria: Judge the edited `review-panel/SKILL.md`. It holds instructions for the executing agent only: no change history, no note of what the skill used to do or why it changed, and no commentary addressed to its author. A reason stays acceptable when it helps the executing agent make a call.

graders.name: no-needless-question
graders.criteria: The request settles what to change: stop after triage and fix only after the user's review and approval. Pass if the agent made the change in `review-panel/SKILL.md` and its final message asks the user nothing the request already settled, such as whether to add the gate or to confirm the edit. A question about something the request leaves open, such as whether verification retries need another approval or whether to offer an auto-fix option, is fine.

graders.name: other-files-unchanged
graders.description: Only the review-panel skill and its README entry change.

graders.name: overview-consistent
graders.criteria: Judge the edited `review-panel/SKILL.md`. Read top to bottom, no part of it still tells the agent to go from triage straight to fixing: the pipeline summary near the top, the triage step, the fix step (which fixes count as accepted) and the report and completion wording all agree with a stop for user approval. The gate itself may be stated once and referred to elsewhere.

graders.name: polish-loaded
graders.description: Process check: refine-it and shorten-it delivered their instructions; this does not show how they were applied.

graders.name: readme
graders.criteria: `README.md` lists review-panel as running a panel that will "merge findings, triage, fix, and verify". Pass if the README entry no longer implies fixes happen without user approval, or the final message points out that the README entry needs that update. Fail if the entry still implies automatic fixes and the final message does not mention it.

graders.name: suggests-check
graders.criteria: The change gates a safeguard, so it warrants one bounded behavior check. Pass if the final message reports running one that exercises the gate, such as a before/after or simulated run in which the agent stops for approval before fixing; a one-line report suffices. Also pass if it names that check and a concrete obstacle to running it. Fail if it only suggests testing, or names a check that does not exercise the stop before fixing.
